Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Art & Design | National Otumfuo pushes for creative industry investment to boost Ghana’s economy Source : Kareen Tei 17 November 2026 11:06am ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
The Asantehene, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II has called for increased investment in Ghana’s creative industry, stressing its potential to generate employment, create wealth and drive economic growth.
He believes the country can unlock greater economic benefits from its arts, fashion and cultural sectors through improved technical training, stronger local production and adequate investment in creative enterprises.
The Asantehene made the call at the Faculty of Applied Arts and Technology (FAAT) Week celebration at Takoradi Technical University (TTU), where he challenged the institution to develop the skills and expertise needed to transform Ghana’s creative industry.
Highlighting the economic potential of the fashion sector, Otumfuo disclosed that the industry was estimated to contribute about GH¢2 billion to the national economy, with considerable room for growth if given the necessary support.
Despite the increasing international recognition of Ghanaian designers and artists, locally manufactured fashion products remain underrepresented in shops and markets, with imported goods continuing to dominate.
“What you cannot find in the shops, though, are Made-in-Ghana labels and sadly, even on the domestic market, our shops are dominated by foreign products, save for the growing indigenous sector,” he observed.
The situation, he said, reflected Ghana’s inability to translate the international recognition of its creative talents into meaningful commercial opportunities for locally manufactured products.
Artists, designers and students were consequently encouraged to prioritise quality, embrace innovation and meet international standards while preserving the country's cultural identity through their work.
Otumfuo also identified the shortage of middle-level technical skills as a major obstacle to industrial development and the expansion of the creative sector.
He tasked Takoradi Technical University with bridging this gap by connecting indigenous knowledge with formal education, experienced artisans with emerging designers, and traditional craftsmanship with modern technology.
“Your university stands at the critical point in the value chain where heritage and culture meet economic value,” he said.
Ghana’s rich traditions in weaving, pottery, metalworking, woodcarving, architecture and visual communication, he stressed, provide a strong foundation for developing a globally competitive creative industry.
Integrating these traditional skills with contemporary design and production techniques would help local artisans and designers develop products capable of competing in international markets.
As part of the celebration, the Asantehene cut the sod for the proposed Otumfuo Osei Tutu II Art Museum at Takoradi Technical University.
The facility is expected to promote artistic expression, preserve Ghana’s cultural heritage and provide a platform for advancing the country's creative arts industry.
The celebration, held under the theme, “Celebrating Heritage, Innovation, and Excellence: A Tribute to Otumfuo Osei Tutu II’s Legacy,” featured cultural performances, an exhibition of artistic creations and a fashion show showcasing designs by students of the Faculty of Applied Arts and Technology.
The Asantehene praised the university for making arts and cultural heritage integral to its academic programmes, urging it to strengthen its role in developing the skilled artists and designers needed to drive Ghana’s creative industry and economic growth.
